synopsis: The booklet uses McNemar's test to compare the old and new warning systems using paired hazard-level hit-or-miss results [f14232, f5481]. Chapter 7 and the glossary require parallel recording on the same machine so both systems encounter the same hazards; separate deployments confound site, operator and weather [f5481, f14233, f14236, f14356]. Only discordant pairs inform the test: hazards caught by both systems or missed by both do not contribute to the comparison [f14234]. The illustrative comparison has 12 hazards caught only by the new system versus 3 caught only by the old, testing whether this imbalance exceeds chance; the supplied facts do not report a test result or significance conclusion [f14235].

relations.note: Both identify same-machine parallel recording as the valid setting for paired testing.
Both require exposure to the same hazards for a valid paired comparison.
Both restrict valid paired testing to shared-event exposure.
Specifies how parallel recording produces hazard-level old-system and new-system hit-or-miss pairs.
Confounding in separate deployments explains the shared-event validity requirement.
Valid use of the comparison requires both systems to record the same hazards simultaneously.
Clarifies that only discordant hazard-level pairs inform McNemar's test.
Provides a numerical example of the paired warning-system comparison.
Illustrates discordant pairs with 12 new-only catches and 3 old-only catches.
Distinguishes the recorded pairs that inform the test from concordant pairs.
